en: n. the act of finishing a course of study at a school or university; a ceremony at which students receive their degrees; a mark on a measuring instrument
ex: Her family attended her graduation ceremony.
她的家人參加了她的畢業典禮。

en: n. the rules of a language that say how words are put together to make sentences; a book that describes these rules; the correct use of a language according to these rules
ex: Learning English grammar is difficult for many students.
學英文文法對許多學生來說很難。

en: a. feeling or showing thanks for something that someone has done for you; pleased and relieved about something; welcome and pleasing
ex: I am grateful for your help with my application.
我很感激你協助我的申請。

en: n. a feeling of being grateful and wanting to thank someone
ex: She wrote a letter to express her gratitude to the teacher.
她寫了一封信向老師表達感激之情。

en: n. a place in the ground where a dead person is buried; a hole in the ground for a coffin; a. serious and worrying; (of a person) serious and solemn; vt. to carve or engrave something
ex: Flowers were placed on the grave of the soldier.
士兵的墳墓上擺放了花束。

en: a. covered with grease or oil; containing a lot of fat or oil; (of a person) unpleasantly friendly
ex: I don't like greasy food like fried chicken.
我不喜歡像炸雞這類油膩的食物。

en: n. words or gestures used to say hello to someone; good wishes sent to someone on a special occasion; a message of good wishes sent on a special day
ex: She sent birthday greetings to her friend in Japan.
她寄了生日賀卡給在日本的朋友。

en: n. a promise that something will be done or will happen; a written promise that a company will repair a product; something that makes something certain; vt. to promise something strongly
ex: This watch comes with a two-year guarantee.
這支手錶有兩年保固。

en: n. a person who is legally responsible for taking care of someone, especially a child; a person who protects or defends something; a. protecting or defending
ex: The child's guardian signed the permission form.
孩子的監護人簽了同意書。

en: n. a feeling of shame because you have done something wrong; the fact of having committed a crime; blame for something
ex: He was filled with guilt after lying to his friend.
他對朋友說謊後充滿愧疚。

en: a. having done something wrong or illegal; feeling or showing guilt; responsible for a wrongdoing
ex: The jury found him guilty of theft.
陪審團裁定他竊盜罪成立。

en: n. a large area of sea partly surrounded by land; a very large difference between two groups or opinions; a deep hole in the ground; vt. to swallow something up
ex: The ship sailed across the Gulf of Mexico.
船航行穿越墨西哥灣。

en: a. done regularly as a habit; usual or typical; (of a person) always doing something
ex: He is a habitual liar and nobody trusts him.
他是慣性說謊者，沒人信任他。

en: n. a situation in which life is very difficult or unpleasant; a thing that makes life very difficult; difficult conditions such as lack of money or food
ex: Many families faced economic hardship during the war.
戰爭期間許多家庭面臨經濟困難。

en: n. a need to do something quickly; the quality of moving quickly; carelessness in doing something because of hurrying
ex: In his haste, he left his umbrella on the bus.
他匆忙中把雨傘忘在公車上。

en: n. an aircraft with large blades on top that spin and lift it off the ground; vt. to transport people or things by helicopter; vi. to travel by helicopter
ex: A rescue helicopter flew over the mountain.
一架救援直升機飛越山頭。

en: n. a structure in which bees live; a place that is full of busy activity; a large group of bees; vi. to enter a hive; vt. to put bees into a hive
ex: The bees returned to the hive at sunset.
蜜蜂在日落時回到蜂巢。

en: n. the country where you were born or where your family comes from; a country that people think of as their home
ex: Many soldiers died defending their homeland.
許多士兵為保衛家園而犧牲。

en: n. all the people who live together in a house; a family and the people who work for it; a. relating to the home; used in the home
ex: The average household has three people.
平均每戶有三個人。

en: n. the work of cleaning and tidying a house and cooking food; jobs done in the house
ex: My husband and I share the housework equally.
我先生和我平均分擔家務。

en: n. all the people in the world considered as a group; the quality of being kind and sympathetic to others; (plural) subjects such as literature and history
ex: The war was a crime against humanity.
那場戰爭是危害人類的罪行。

en: n. the amount of water in the air; the state of being damp; moisture in the atmosphere
ex: The humidity is very high in summer here.
這裡夏天的濕度很高。

en: n. a violent storm with strong winds that forms over warm water in the Atlantic Ocean; a very strong wind; a situation with lots of trouble
ex: The hurricane destroyed many houses along the coast.
颶風摧毀了沿岸許多房屋。

en: n. a colorless gas that is the lightest element and burns easily; the most common element in the universe
ex: Water is made of hydrogen and oxygen.
水是由氫和氧組成的。

en: n. a document that proves who you are; the act of recognizing someone or something; a feeling of being closely connected to someone
ex: You need to show identification to enter the building.
進入大樓需要出示身分證件。

en: vt. to recognize someone or something and say who or what they are; to find the cause or origin of something; to connect someone with something; vi. to feel that you share something with someone
ex: The witness could not identify the thief.
目擊者無法指認出小偷。

en: a. not working or active; not busy; lazy and not willing to work; having no particular purpose or value; vi. (of an engine) to run slowly without moving; to spend time doing nothing
ex: The factory has been idle since the strike began.
罷工開始後，工廠就一直停工。

en: n. a picture or drawing in a book or magazine; an example that explains or proves something; the act of making something clear with examples
ex: The book has many colorful illustrations.
這本書有許多彩色插圖。

en: a. existing only in the mind and not in reality; not real; made up
ex: The child had an imaginary friend named Bobo.
那孩子有一個叫波波的想像朋友。

en: vt. to copy the way someone behaves, speaks or looks; to make something that looks like something else; to follow someone's example
ex: The parrot can imitate human voices.
那隻鸚鵡會模仿人類的聲音。

en: n. a person who has come to live in a foreign country; a. relating to people who have come to a new country
ex: Her grandparents were immigrants from Italy.
她的祖父母是來自義大利的移民。

en: vi. to come to live permanently in a foreign country; vt. to bring people into a country to live there permanently
ex: Her family immigrated to Canada in 1990.
她的家人在 1990 年移民到加拿大。

en: n. a strong effect or influence on something; the force of one object hitting another; vt. to have an effect on something; to press something firmly into another thing
ex: The new law will have a big impact on small businesses.
新法律將對小企業造成很大影響。

en: vt. to force someone to accept something; to officially introduce a rule or tax; to take advantage of someone's kindness; vi. to take unfair advantage of someone
ex: The government imposed a new tax on cigarettes.
政府對香菸課徵新稅。

en: n. a sign that shows that something is happening or is true; a statement or action that shows what is likely to happen; a reading on a measuring instrument
ex: There is no indication that he is lying.
沒有跡象顯示他在說謊。

en: n. a general increase in prices; the act of making something larger by filling it with air or gas; the act of making something seem more important than it really is
ex: Inflation has made everything more expensive.
通貨膨脹使一切都變貴了。

en: a. giving a lot of useful information; helping you to understand something; educational
ex: The documentary was very informative about marine life.
那部紀錄片對海洋生物提供了很多資訊。

en: a. happening at the beginning; first; n. the first letter of a name; vt. to mark something with your initials
ex: My initial reaction was one of surprise.
我最初的反應是驚訝。

en: vt. to hurt someone or something physically; to harm someone's feelings or reputation; to cause damage to something
ex: He injured his leg while playing football.
他踢足球時傷到了腿。

en: n. the state of not being guilty of a crime; lack of knowledge or experience of the world; the quality of being pure and without any bad intention
ex: The man proved his innocence in court.
那男子在法庭上證明了自己的清白。
